texts.orig: A confounding variable is the quality of PMs these companies hire. If a company hires only amazing senior PMs, they will naturally go on to do amazing things—and that doesn’t mean the company made these PMs great. However, if the goal of this post is to help you figure out where to work, getting a gig at one of the companies on this list will put you on a good track either way.

texts.orig: Based on the data we have available to us, the best proxy we found for measuring “successful” was to look at which companies have gone on to raise a Series A. Yes, some founders choose to stay bootstrapped and never raise money, and raising a Series A doesn’t mean you’re successful, but it’s a simple way to zero in on founders aiming to build large venture-scale companies.

texts.text: Why didn’t Stripe PMs do better?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In this analysis and the previous edition, I was stumped as to why Stripe didn’t perform better. I’ve been nothing but impressed with every PM I’ve ever met from Stripe, and I’ve had more Stripe and ex-Stripe people on my podcast than any other company. WTF.
texts.text: In this analysis and the previous edition, I was stumped as to why Stripe didn’t perform better. I’ve been nothing but impressed with every PM I’ve ever met from Stripe, and I’ve had more Stripe and ex-Stripe people on my podcast than any other company. WTF.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It turns out Stripe’s PMs get hired to be star PMs at rocketship companies. Instead of starting their own companies or climbing the ladder, they go on to become key PMs at top companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Mercury, Adyen, Scale, etc.
texts.text: It turns out Stripe’s PMs get hired to be star PMs at rocketship companies. Instead of starting their own companies or climbing the ladder, they go on to become key PMs at top companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Mercury, Adyen, Scale, etc.
